newsitem.title: USA: Algeria eyes new LPG plant to pace with production.
newsitem.headline: Algeria eyes new LPG plant to pace with production.

text.p: The head of Algeria's state-owned oil and gas company said Wednesday the country is looking to build another huge gas processing complex to keep pace with natural gas and oil production.
Speaking at an economic conference on Algeria in New York, Sonatrach head Nazim Zouioueche said the $4 billion complex would take about four years to build.
He did not give details on the complex's capacity or whether foreign investment as seen on such scales as in Algeria's other upstream and downstream operations would be involved.
"We are thinking about a new LNG plant in Algeria but as of now nothing serious has developed at the moment," Zouioueche told the Citibank-hosted meeting.
In the past decade, foreign companies have played a large role in developing and expanding Algeria's oil and gas operations, investing more than 1.3 billion dollars.

This year alone, Sonatrach has signed five contracts with BP, Arco, Total-Repsol, Agip and Petronas to develop oil and gas projects, including pipelines and the huge fields of Hassi Berkine and Berkine Est-Ourhourd.
Zouioueche said the state-owned concern is open to more downstream and upstream partnerships.
"Opportunities for partnership (with Sonatrach) are numerous and attractive," Zouioueche said, adding the concern and its partners will invest around 17.8 billion between 1996 and 2000.
Development of the $4 billion gas processing plant is to help the country keep up with a near doubling by 2010 of its oil and gas production.

Total hydrocarbon production, according to Zouioueche, is expected to increase from 167 million tonnes in 1995 to 210 million tonnes in 2000. More than half of the country's 36 billion barrels of proven hydrocarbon reserves are of natural gas, a main feedstock for Algerian liquid petroleum gases.
Potentially, the country has 105 billion barrels of hydrocarbons in its fields.
LPG production is also expected to increase due to expansions and work at two plants, from a current six million tonnes to 8.4 million by 1998.
LPG exports are expected to double, from 3.5 million tonnes in 1995 to 8.4 million tonne by 2000, said Zouioueche.

Sonatrach sells to 20 countries, of which the Mediterranean, with 54 percent of all sales, the U.S. with 21 percent and Brazil with 10 percent are the most important markets. The company has said it will continue to sell the same percentages as output grows.
